messages.author: e64f7bb1494774f9
messages.subject: Genetic diversity
parts:
Hi All,

Does anyone know how to extract individual genetic diversity scores from either: 
gl.diversity()
or
gl.report.heterozygosity() 

These functions are great, but instead of averaging over the population, I would like to extract scores per individual in my sample populations. It is also unclear if either of these functions standardizes for sample size? I

Alternatively, I am happy to use another function more suitable for calculating different metrics of genetic diversity at the individual level.

Thanks in advance!

messages.author: a3ea45e87285d820
messages.subject: Re: Genetic diversity
parts:
Hi Kate,

I think that the heterozygosity script outputs the heterozyosities for you, e.g.

Starting gl.report.heterozygosity 
  Warning: genlight object contains monomorphic loci
  Calculating Observed Heterozygosities, averaged across loci, for each population
  Calculating Expected Heterozygosities, averaged across loci, for each population
Completed: gl.report.heterozygosity 
                pop nInd  nLoc       Ho   Ho.adj       He   He.adj
1     EmmacBrisWive   10 225.4 0.005784 0.005784 0.009224 0.009224
2     EmmacBurdMist   10 224.6 0.004920 0.004920 0.005105 0.005105
3     EmmacBurnBara   11 225.9 0.013269 0.013269 0.015370 0.015370
4     EmmacClarJack    5 219.2 0.004490 0.004490 0.005923 0.005923
5     EmmacClarYate    5 223.6 0.004421 0.004421 0.004333 0.004333
6     EmmacCoopAvin   10 195.9 0.008707 0.008707 0.008990 0.008990
7    EmmacCoopCully   10 232.6 0.005156 0.005156 0.004958 0.004958
8     EmmacCoopEulb   10 221.9 0.004054 0.004054 0.006048 0.006048

I guess the best way to get what you want would be to assign each individual as a population, using

gl <- gl.reassign.pop(testset.gl,as.pop="id")
popNames(gl)
out <- gl.report.heterozygosity(gl)
out

I do not think the scripts weight the contribution of loci or of individuals for sample size (takes the means of the means). This is something we should consider for a future release.

A

messages.author: b3d929c6746ca81a
messages.subject: RE: [dartR] Genetic diversity
parts:
Hi Kate,

 

Unfortunately both answer are no.

 

It is on my growing list to correct for sample sizes, but not implemented yet.

 

What potentially could work if you define your populations as being individuals, but not sure if it does not break the code for some routines in the function. But potentially it might work for some indices on the individual level doing that. (as I said not tested).

 

Eg.

pop(gl) <- indNames(gl)

 

and then

 

divs <- gl.diversiyt(gl)

 

As I said not sure if it works but I put the request on my todo list.

 

Cheers, Bernd

messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Genetic diversity
parts:
Hi Arthur and Bernd,

Thank you for the incredibly fast response! 

I can confirm that the following works to calculate diversity metrics for individuals within a population. Very nice hack :)

gl <- gl.reassign.pop(testset.gl,as.pop="id")

popNames(gl)

out <- gl.report.heterozygosity(gl)

Both of you mentioned the incorporation of standardizing sampling size of either 1) population or 2) loci as being on the "to-do list." Some thoughts below to hopefully make it easier for you?

1) Bashalkhanov's model: this paper developed and validated (with natural population data) a metric for this: “A simple method for estimating genetic diversity in large populations from finite sample sizes: Bashalkhanov et al. BMC Genetics 2009, 10:84doi:10.1186/1471-2156-10-84.

Perhaps this model could be incorporated, loops through all the SNPs, and applies a correction at the end for multiple comparisons (Bonferroni)? 

 

2) Could borrow from the microbial literature that routinely calculates diversity metrics across samples of varying read abundance. Rarefaction used to be the norm but now negative binomial and zero-inflated Gaussian mixture models (package metagenomeSeq) are now being used within the wonderful Phyloseq package.

Waste Not, Want Not: Why Rarefying Microbiome Data Is Inadmissible, McMurdie and Holmes https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003531

 

3) The following are quick and dirty but not ideal:

H0/nLoc

H0/nInd per population

 

Anyways, thank you for the help 😊

Cheers,

Kate

messages.author: a3ea45e87285d820
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Genetic diversity
parts:
Thanks Kate.

Hack!! It is a feature :)

Will look at those papers. They look interesting, though allelic richness could be a challenge with SNP data (all loci have only  one or two alleles).

The current way dartR calculates Heterozygosity is to calculate it for each locus, then averages across loci for each individual, then averages across individuals for an estimate for the population. Clearly this will weight loci equally, even though they differ in call rate. Not a big problem if you filter heavily on call rate (say, threshold = 0.95).

I think I can easily add an option to weight the heterozygosity at a locus for call rate, then average over individuals to get a sample-size-weighted estimate for the population.

I will look at this more carefully as soon as I get a chance.

A
